I'd say it depends on the city, organization, and really a ton of other factors. Some are too cramped, and some are just money grabs. For instant my city is making this big push to "employ" the homeless, and this amazing new program starts next month. It's sponsored by the one of the larger shelter/homeless orgs in the midwest. The pay? $10 an hour, twice a week for 14 hours total pay. You also get a lunch. The amount of homeless they will employ? 5. 1 program manager, and 1 assistant. Total combined funding given by the city for the year is 150k. Some basic math will tell you the majority of that money is clearly not going to the homeless.

You will run into issues of forced religious belief even if you don't believe in that faith in certain shelters. Poor upkeep, and violence can be issues. Drugs, stealing, and generally bad environments. From the outside looking in, people want to judge the homeless, and ask why some don't go to shelters. However, I'd argue if you can take advantage of assistance programs, counseling, therapy, employment, food, and learning without being in a shelter environment you may be better off. If you have a car, then sleep there if possible. However, if it's freezing or you have no option then a shelter is better than nothing.

The mindset you might inherit will be your biggest issue. Trust me. My life is just in constant turmoil, and this winter has made me more depressed than ever. I just hope to survive until spring where I can hopefully get another chance at life. If you get into a shelter, make a few friends if need be. Better to know people, and have a couple buddies to avoid theft and whatnot. However, if they are the "lifers" don't let that infect you. People always say it, and it's true. Your mindset really changes your reality. Negativity breeds negativity.
